# R17 safe power-off (generated by `python -m rnd.power_off`)

Question: on a loss of torque (e-stop, a latched fault, power loss: the drives are disabled, the contactor is open) the D25
people-near soft limit (shoulder roll ≥ +5°, sw/safety.py) is gone. Where does each arm joint go, can the inboard
shoulder-roll wedge (yaw band / block against the arm-side ferrule: ≈ 2.5 mm at −15°, ≥ 25 mm from ≈ +1°, rnd/pinch.py)
close, and what is the cheapest mechanical guarantee?

Method. The twin (rnd/twin.py, both arms, CAD masses) with the drives off: each joint gets its back-drive torque as
Coulomb friction (MuJoCo frictionloss) and its reflected rotor inertia as armature (rnd/inline_study.py joint_drive:
N·τ_drag/η_b + gearbox breakaway, ESTIMATE, ×0.5…×2 swept), no damping (phases open: the drive's MCU is unpowered,
ESTIMATE), the shoulder balancer τ = K·sin(pitch) (K = params arm.spring_k_nm, rnd/balancer.py), the lift held by its
spring-applied pawl (lift.md option C), the joint limits at the hard stops (roll −16.5 / +104°, rnd/parts/roll.py
STOP_AT; the others at the soft limit + 3°, ESTIMATE). Start poses are sampled in the states the supervisor allows:
**people near** (roll ≥ +8°: the +5° bound + the 3° margin; both hands inside PERSON_WS, intersected with LOAD_WS above
1 kg) and **nobody near** (roll in the −12…+5° band the soft limit removes, hands in the free workspace / LOAD_WS), at
rest, with 0 / 1 kg (one hand) / 2.5 kg / the 9.07 kg R2d basket (two hands, half each). Each start is let go for
T_SIM s. Contacts are off (the links may pass through each other and the base: joint limits only), so a fall that would
end on the base is reported as passing through it (ESTIMATE: a fall that lands on the base stops earlier). Gripper:
not modelled (an unpowered STS3215 gripper's hold on the payload is not demonstrated: R17 open item).

## Back-drive model (drives off)

| Joint | Actuator | Ratio | Back-drive torque (N·m, mid; ×0.5…×2) | Viscous (N·m·s/rad, twin datasheet) | Reflected rotor inertia (kg·m²) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| pitch | GIM6010-8 | 24:1 |0.64 (0.32…1.28) | 2 | 0.0138 |
| roll | GIM8108-36 | 36:1 |0.94 (0.47…1.88) | 2 | 0.0778 |
| yaw | GIM6010-8 | 16:1 |0.44 (0.22…0.89) | 1 | 0.0061 |
| elbow | GIM6010-8 | 16:1 |0.44 (0.22…0.89) | 1 | 0.0061 |
| wpitch | DM-J4310-2EC_V1.1 | 10:1 |0.15 (0.08…0.31) | 0.5 | 0.0006 |
| wroll | STS3215-C018 |  |0.50 (0.25…1.00) | 0.3 | 0.0000 |

Shoulder balancer K = 4.5 N·m (τ = K·sin pitch): it cancels about half of the straight-arm gravity moment, so pitch is never held by it alone. Lift: spring-applied pawl, held. Hard stops: roll -16.5 / 104° (roll.py STOP_AT), the others ±3° past the soft limits (ESTIMATE).

**Reading.** Unpowered, pitch falls to hanging (balancer 4.5 N·m against ≈ 10–17 N·m of arm + load), the elbow straightens below it, and the roll comes to rest wherever its gravity torque drops under the back-drive friction: a band of a few degrees about hanging (roll ≈ 0). From the people-near poses (roll ≥ +8°) the roll got down to **-16.7°** (9.07 kg, back-drive ×1, viscous ×0): the wedge at **1 mm**; 100% of the starts in the worst set ended under 25 mm. From the band the soft limit removes (only allowed with nobody near), the arm stays in it. Either way **nothing holds it there**: the push table below.

## Pushing the unpowered arm

Hand force that back-drives the roll inward from hanging (arm straight down, lift top): back-drive friction minus any gravity torque already pushing inward, over the hand's lever about the roll axis. *Finger force* = what a 20 N push at the hand puts on a finger in the wedge (lever ratio, wedge at r ≈ 70 mm).

| Load | Roll at rest | Back-drive × | Hand lever (m) | Push to close (N) | Finger force at a 20 N push (N) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 kg | +5° | 1 | 0.74 | 0.1 | 210 |
| 0 kg | +0° | 0.5 | 0.74 | 0.6 | 210 |
| 0 kg | +0° | 1 | 0.74 | 1.3 | 210 |
| 0 kg | +0° | 2 | 0.74 | 2.6 | 210 |
| 0 kg | -5° | 1 | 0.74 | 2.4 | 210 |
| 1 kg | +5° | 1 | 0.74 | 0.0 | 210 |
| 1 kg | +0° | 0.5 | 0.74 | 0.6 | 210 |
| 1 kg | +0° | 1 | 0.74 | 1.3 | 210 |
| 1 kg | +0° | 2 | 0.74 | 2.6 | 210 |
| 1 kg | -5° | 1 | 0.74 | 3.3 | 210 |
| 2.5 kg | +5° | 1 | 0.74 | 0.0 | 210 |
| 2.5 kg | +0° | 0.5 | 0.74 | 0.6 | 210 |
| 2.5 kg | +0° | 1 | 0.74 | 1.3 | 210 |
| 2.5 kg | +0° | 2 | 0.74 | 2.6 | 210 |
| 2.5 kg | -5° | 1 | 0.74 | 3.5 | 210 |

## Options (mechanical guarantee)

| | Option | Guarantee | Cost | Mass | Reach (R16: top-down / 45° / side / across-body; targets 30/63/62/54 %) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| O0 | Today: D25 software soft limit only | none unpowered: the arm rests anywhere in the roll friction band (≈ ±3…6° about hanging) and a few N at the hand closes the wedge | $0 | 0 | full 35%/78%/78%/71% (R16 ✅) with nobody near; 17%/57%/67%/49% with a person near |
| O1 | Fixed hard stop at +5° (the −16.5° bush moved: STOP_AT[0] = +5°) | all states, powered or not, any push | ≈ $0 (geometry change; the bushes, plate and arm-rear half-width re-derive from STOP_AT) | 0 | 17%/57%/67%/49% **always** (3 of 4 R16 targets missed; across-body −22 points) |
| O2 | **Spring-applied latch at +5°, solenoid-retracted** (Ø10 hardened pin in a steel guide bush in the rear plate, on the same arm edge as the −16.5° bush; 24 V pull solenoid fed from the K1-switched bus through a supervisor-gated FET; pin-retracted switch) | every state that starts at roll ≥ +5°: people near (the soft limit keeps it there), and every unpowered state that began there; the pin drops in by spring the moment K1 opens or the supervisor drops it. Residual: an unplanned loss of power while the arm is in the −16.5…+5° band with nobody near (the pin rests on the arm face until the arm next rises past +5°) | ≈ $14 per arm (solenoid $6–9, pin + bush $3, spring $0.5, hall switch + magnet $2, FET + wiring $1; ESTIMATE) → ≈ $28 robot | ≈ 45 g per arm (ESTIMATE) | full 35%/78%/78%/71% with nobody near; 17%/57%/67%/49% with a person near or unpowered (as D25 today) |
| O2b | O2 + band spring (a 5–8 N·m spring plunger acting only over −16.5…+6°, pushes the unpowered arm out of the band onto the latch) | all unpowered states (the arm leaves the band in ≲ 0.5 s, then the latch holds); push-proof once latched | O2 + ≈ $3 | O2 + ≈ 15 g | as O2, but the roll motor holds the spring (≈ 5–8 of 35 N·m) while working in the band |
| O3 | Spring-applied friction brake on the roll output (≥ 1.5 × the worst roll gravity torque) | holds gravity + payload at any angle; a push above the brake torque still closes the wedge | ≈ $60–120 per arm (no catalogue power-off brake fits round the Ø96 motor in the 121 × 96 dome; a custom caliper on the Ø76 adapter needs ≈ 1 kN spring clamp; ESTIMATE) | ≈ 0.3–0.6 kg per arm (ESTIMATE) | none |
| O4 | Geometry: roll axis ≈ +23 mm outboard (ROLL_Y), wedge ≥ 25 mm at −15° (pinch.md) | all states | redesign; ≈ $0 parts | ≈ +40 g per arm (longer roll link / ferrule boss; ESTIMATE) | ≈ none (R16 to re-run); +46 mm shoulder span against the R5 70 cm door (folded arms already 0.70–0.78 m, tip.md) |
| O5 | Bias spring only (no latch): outward spring torque over the whole band | stops gravity closing the wedge, not a push; the unpowered arm settles at the band's edge (≈ +5°) with nothing holding it there | ≈ $3 | ≈ 15 g | as O2b (motor torque in the band) |

## Latch sizing (O1 / O2)

Unpowered fall onto a +5° stop, per load (people-near starts, back-drive ×1): contact speed from the runs, J = the twin's roll inertia hanging (rotor 0.078 kg·m² included), stop stiffness steel 2 kN/mm or PU-capped 0.2 kN/mm at r 42 mm (ESTIMATE); overshoot = how far past +5° the arm presses in.

| Load | Contact speed (rad/s) | J (kg·m²) | Gravity in (N·m) | Steel: peak N·m / kN, overshoot ° → wedge mm | PU cap: peak N·m / kN, overshoot ° → wedge mm |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 kg | 0.60 | 0.51 | 5.6 | 31 / 0.74, 0.5° → 30 | 14 / 0.33, 2.2° → 27 |
| 1 kg | 0.76 | 1.05 | 7.8 | 54 / 1.29, 0.9° → 29 | 22 / 0.54, 3.6° → 25 |
| 2.5 kg | 0.80 | 1.18 | 7.5 | 59 / 1.41, 1.0° → 29 | 24 / 0.57, 3.9° → 25 |
| 9.07 kg | 5.81 | 2.96 | 13.7 | 608 / 14.48, 9.9° → 17 | 202 / 4.80, 32.7° → 1 |

Powered fault into the pin: rated 35 N·m → 0.84 kN, stall 103 N·m → 2.45 kN (what the fixed −16.5 / +104° bushes are sized for: clamped by their M4 to the motor face, roll.drive_capacity). **Design (CAD behind PIP_ROLL_GUARD=latch, rnd/parts/roll.py LATCH):** Ø10 hardened head (5 mm into the arm's 8 mm edge, ISO 8734-style dowel, bending at 2.45 kN × 5 mm ≈ 125 MPa) guided by its hole in the 7075 rear plate and a Ø11.5 42CrMo4 sleeve in the roll-link floor, a Ø6 stem in the cup ring to the spring and a pull cable to a 24 V solenoid in the side block; retract stroke 8 mm (pin centre at roll -48.2°, r 41.5 mm; 4.2 mm to the nearest screw sleeve / bush, 1.45 / 1.45 mm plate ring walls, 0.75 mm print outside the sleeve, 0.9 mm to the driver pilot; the arm covers the pin over roll -16…4°). **Its weak link is the print behind the sleeve** (≈ 0.4 kN at 12 MPa), not the pin: sw/safety.py caps the roll torque at LATCH_T_MAX = 16 N·m (0.39 kN) while the pin may be in (people near, faults: there the drive only has to hold the arm, ≤ 14 N·m with the basket); with the PU cap the unpowered falls stay ≤ 0.4 kN up to 0 kg and reach 0.54 kN at 1 kg, 0.57 kN at 2.5 kg, 4.80 kN at 9.07 kg. So a metal path to the motor face (a flanged sleeve clamped under the two neighbouring M4) is the open detail before the latch can be credited for loaded falls or a stall; falls with the 9 kg basket are also where SW-T7 (basket only with the area clear, rnd/tip.py) does the work.

**Supervisor half (sw/safety.py item 16; `roll_latch`, on with PIP_ROLL_GUARD=latch, default off):** `roll_latch_solenoid()` is energised (pin retracted) only while the supervisor is healthy and nobody is near; until the pin-retracted switch confirms (`set_latch_switch`), or LATCH_RETRACT_S (50 ms) without one, the roll target stays ≥ the +5° bound (+3° margin, never above the arm); a person near or any latched fault drops the pin at once; the roll torque is capped at LATCH_T_MAX while the pin may be in; ROLL_PARK_DEG (+8°) is where the planner parks the roll when idle or before a planned power-down (closes most of O2's residual window). Hardware half (electrical track): the solenoid is fed from the K1-switched bus through a supervisor-gated FET, so e-stop / K1 open drops it whatever the software does; one GPIO in, one out. Tested in sw/test_s1.py test_roll_latch.

**Recommendation (owner's call):** O2 (latch) if the across-body / top-down reach with nobody near matters; O1 if a permanent R16 loss is acceptable (it is free and has no residual); add O2b if the band residual (unplanned power loss with the arm across the body and nobody near) is not acceptable. O3 and O5 do not stop a push; O4 spends the door width. Bench: the roll back-drive torque (both directions, hot and cold), the latch's drop time (spring only) and a dummy-load fall onto the pin.

Not covered here: the unpowered pitch fall itself (peak hand speeds above are an impact / crush hazard of their own: Astra's "load-rated power-loss arrest" applies to pitch too; a phase-short at the pitch drive slows it but does not hold it), the gripper's hold on the payload, and the lift (pawl).
